idiom_name: sealed token enum + precedence function, recursive climb or operator stack
implementation_notes: Scala's local idiom is a sealed token enum plus a precedence function, with reduction expressed either as a recursive climb or as an explicit operator stack: the Scala 3 compiler does the latter - precedence(operatorName) feeds reduceStack, which pops while the stacked operator binds tighter (or equally, for left-associative names) and checks associativity, keeping source offsets in an OpInfo stack. Scala 3's own infix-method precedence and infix modifier govern how Scala code calls methods, not how your grammar resolves operators, so the table stays yours to define while pattern matching on the sealed hierarchy keeps dispatch exhaustive. Reach for scala-parser-combinators or fastparse once the grammar outgrows its expression layer, accepting that generated-combinator diagnostics are less precise than hand-written ones.
code_sketch:
def precedence(name: String): Int = name.head match
  case '*' | '/' => 20
  case '+' | '-' => 10
  case _         => 5

def expr(min: Int): Expr =
  var left = primary()                                  // null denotation
  while precedence(peekName) >= min do                  // left denotation
    val op = consume().name
    val right = expr(precedence(op) + 1)                // left-associative
    left = Bin(op, left, right)
  left
pitfalls: Scala's infix-method precedence is a language rule keyed on the first character of the method name, and Scala 3 adds the infix modifier; copying that rule into your parser is a modelling mistake unless the DSL deliberately mirrors Scala semantics.

An explicit operator stack must decide equal-precedence associativity explicitly - left-associative pops while precedence >= top, right-associative while > top - and getting it backwards is invisible until chained operators are tested.
The compiler's own parser carries source positions and error offsets through the stack; a hand-rolled version that drops them produces diagnostics without locations.
